A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same depth-learning system and experimental program. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete supplementary material support comparison despite substantial presentation changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original depth-benchmark results, computational-efficiency measurements, online-learning outcomes, and drone flight experiments, including supplementary qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original benchmark and flight results and additionally reports a ground-truth-depth flight comparison and intervention-distance distributions.

M1.justification: The 430,416-parameter architecture, contrast-maximization and geometry losses, parallel CUDA processing, and depth-based yaw controller remain unchanged. The expanded thread and gradient descriptions explain the existing implementation rather than establish a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVSEC, DSEC, UZH-FPV, and the same indoor drone-navigation setting. The four supplementary flight scenes are retained. Discussion of dynamic obstacles and natural environments does not introduce evaluations in those scenarios.

E2.justification: V2 Figures 5 and 7 add navigation using RealSense ground-truth depth alongside training from scratch, pre-training, and pre-training plus online learning. The comparator sets in benchmark Tables 1–2 and the computational-efficiency comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Flight evaluation adds a ground-truth-depth control and replaces intervention-time percentages with distance between interventions. Flight MAE is described as depth error in meters rather than disparity error. The changed learning-step axis does not establish an actual increase in training budget.

E4.justification: The added ground-truth-depth flight control tests whether better perception eliminates interventions; remaining corner failures help distinguish controller limitations from depth-estimation limitations. Existing online-learning comparisons and supplementary qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: V2 Figure 5 adds boxplots showing the distribution of distances between interventions, whereas v1 reports aggregate intervention-time percentages. No new seed counts, repeated-training-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 retain their scores. Flight reporting replaces 50%, 35%, and 11% intervention times with annotated distances of 2.20, 3.61, 4.66, and 11.75 meters for TFS, PT, PT+OL, and ground truth. Figure 2's efficiency curves are updated, and main-text power consumption changes from 15 W to 9 W, matching the retained appendix table.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the static-scene assumption, warping relationships, and geometry-consistency formulation are retained. Added event definitions and gradient explanations do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain on-device self-supervised depth learning and improved obstacle avoidance. V2 narrows the conclusion's memory-saving claim from 100× to 2–5×, expresses navigation benefit as approximately 30% greater distance between interventions, and claims applicability to other warping/splatting pipelines.

C2.justification: V1 mainly discusses benchmark accuracy limitations and the supervised-learning gap. V2 substantially expands deployment limitations: reduced resolution, dependence on artificial texture, depth underestimation for approaching objects, and controller failures at corners or in denser environments. It also discusses specific computational and modeling alternatives as possible remedies.

D1.justification: V2 adds a project-page URL, CUDA thread and backward-gradient details, the efficiency benchmark's 10% padding specification, controller constants, fixed-height flight at 0.5 m/s, and receiver hardware information. These are primarily newly disclosed details; the architecture and training recipe remain stable.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of UFO Depth and Depth Distillation, attributes architectural inspiration to Wu et al., and adds references connecting potential extensions to reconstruction, continual learning, and other splatting applications. The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Editing and restructuring span the main text and supplement: the abstract and conclusion are rewritten, related-work subsections become run-in headings, experiments gain Setup/Results/Limitations divisions, and supplementary sections are consolidated into qualitative results and implementation details.

P2.justification: V2 redesigns Figure 1, incorporates a redrawn version of v1's supplementary warping illustration into Figure 2, reorganizes flight plots, and adds ground-truth trajectories. Event-input rows supplement retained qualitative predictions, and the architecture and hardware tables are placed together.

improvement.justification: The ground-truth control, distributional flight results, controller details, and explicit deployment limitations make the existing demonstration more interpretable and reproducible. Corrected memory and power claims improve calibration. These gains are tempered by unclear learning-step labeling: v2 Figure 5 uses a 0–12k axis while retaining a caption stating that 300 steps correspond to 100 seconds.
